summary.headline: UltraTech Q1 FY27: domestic grey volume up 13.1% to 81% utilisation, EBITDA INR5,146 crore and PAT INR2,604 crore (+17.2%).
summary.overview: The document is headed India Cements Ltd but the enclosed transcript is UltraTech Cement's Q1 FY27 earnings call (held 20 July 2026), with CFO Atul Daga presenting. Domestic grey cement volume grew 13.1% YoY, with capacity utilisation at 81% versus 76%, and revenue rose 16%. Management flagged a fuel and packing cost shock during the quarter and guided to a further INR130-140 per ton cost increase in Q2 FY27. India Cements turnaround continued, with EBITDA per ton at INR603 versus roughly INR386 in Q2 FY26, and Cables and Wires remains on track for Q3 FY27 launch.

financial_highlights.value: About INR12 per bag average from INR9
financial_highlights.change: up about INR3/bag average in quarter

financial_highlights.metric: India Cements revenue (ex-factory, net of freight)

financial_highlights.change: from about INR386 in Q2 FY26, INR400 and INR509 in intervening quarters

segments.name: Grey cement (UltraTech incl. India Cements and Kesoram)
segments.commentary: Domestic volume up 13.1% with 81% utilisation on a 200 mtpa base; brand growth of 21.3%. East was the slowest region in the quarter, South and North were just below 15%, West and Central above 15%.

segments.name: India Cements (turnaround)
segments.commentary: Brand migration to UltraTech is 100% complete; revenue up 21% and volume up 19% like-for-like; conversion ratio 1.5x. Management targets INR1,000 per ton EBITDA with the full capex benefit from Q4 FY28.

segments.name: Cables and Wires
segments.commentary: INR1,800 crore programme with INR888 crore spent or committed to date; commissioning and product launch reaffirmed for Oct-Dec 2026 quarter (Q3 FY27).

guidance_outlook: Management is targeting double-digit grey cement volume growth for FY27.
Industry volume growth in Q1 FY27 estimated at 7-8% (management's marketing intelligence), though 'too early'.
Q2 FY27 cost increase guided at INR130-140 per ton (fuel, maintenance, operating deleverage, monsoon), with measures planned to absorb part of it.
Industry expects cement prices to hold broadly steady through the monsoon quarter; management said it will attempt higher prices.
Capacity to reach 212.7 mtpa grey by end FY27 and about 235 mtpa by March 2028; consolidated capacity beyond 242 mtpa.
Management expects a better H2 FY27 cost position if the West Asia conflict eases; India Cements EBITDA of INR1,000 per ton remains the target, with full benefit from Q4 FY28.
Company does not give formal Cables and Wires guidance; net debt to EBITDA expected to remain below 1x for FY27.
capex_capacity: Domestic capacity at 200.1 mtpa and total capacity 205.5 mtpa after commissioning of 8.7 mt of UltraTech capacity (Shahjahanpur, Visakhapatnam, Patratu) in the quarter.
Projects under execution backed by about INR17,000 crore capex over the next 2-2.5 years; all growth capex funded from internal accruals.
Green power at 1,897 MW (about 47% of power requirement at quarter end); 71 MW renewables and 19 MW WHRS commissioned in the quarter; target 2.5-3 GW shortly.
India Cements cost-improvement capex of about INR2,000 crore (WHR, preheater and cooler upgrades); green power share to rise from about 3% to about 86% by end FY28.
Lead distance down to 360 km from 367 km; AFR substitution ramping up.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as strong and broadening, citing infrastructure, housing, urban real estate, ports, data centres and metro projects.
All-India exit prices improved through June; East and South led increases, Central and West steady, North consistent.
Premiumisation and blended cement mix support blended realisations; RMC is about 3.5% of UltraTech sales and retail about 65-66%.
Blended coal cost was USD134/ton in the quarter (INR1.9/kcal cited); currently about INR2/kcal and inventory-loaded.
Diesel (industrial) rose from about INR78-80/litre pre-war to about INR150-157, lifting limestone raising costs by about 13-14% QoQ per the raw material index.
Pet coke now costlier than coal on an energy basis, so coal is preferred.

qa_highlights.question: How will growing operating cash flow be deployed across dividends and cement capex, and will cables and wires capex scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash flows are fully booked for growth capex and dividends; no further cables and wires investment is foreseen for now, with the business first maturing.

qa_highlights.question: What remains before India Cements is merged into a standalone entity?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex programme completion and disposal of non-core land are pending; the journey is expected to complete in Q4 FY28 or a quarter earlier, with some operating parameters still to bring in line.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 FY27 cost impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost increase of INR130-140 per ton expected in Jul-Sep quarter, covering fuel, maintenance, deleverage; Q1 one-off impact was about INR40 on fuel and about INR20 on bags.

qa_highlights.question: Regional demand trends?
qa_highlights.answer: East was slowest in April-June (elections, labour availability); South and North below 15%; West and Central above 15%. East expected to see a multi-year upcycle.

qa_highlights.question: Industry volume growth for the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Estimated at 7-8% based on marketing intelligence; management noted it is early.

qa_highlights.question: Growth beyond 240 mtpa and inorganic options?
qa_highlights.answer: Inorganic opportunities will be examined; the team is working on plans beyond 240 mtpa and details will follow.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict and fuel cost volatility: crude above USD100 at the start of the quarter, with ocean freight insurance up to 4-5% from under 1%.
Q2 FY27 margin pressure of INR130-140/ton from fuel, maintenance and monsoon deleverage; watch whether management absorbs part of it.
Monsoon and dry spells (Rajasthan, some other states) could affect rural demand and next-year water-linked construction.
Cables and Wires: Q3 FY27 launch timeline, working capital build-up over the next 6 months, and ramp-up.
Industry capacity plans may be revised, per management comments on the 2027-28 industry capacity number.
India Cements per-ton EBITDA trajectory towards INR1,000/t and the India Cements merger timeline (Q4 FY28).
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional, with strong emphasis on demand, brand and track record. Management was candid on near-term cost pressure but gave few hard numbers on the longer term; it deflected several questions (e.g., cables and wires guidance, challenges over 5 years, capacity additions by the industry).
key_quotes: We intend to grow like a challenger and not an incumbent.
We absorbed the shock better than any peer, and we will harvest the relief faster than any peer.
We said we will cross 200 million tons; we did a year early.
Yes, we are targeting double-digit volume growth this year.

Cables and Wires INR1,800 crore programme, commissioning and launch Oct-Dec 2026

growth.why: Management targets double-digit grey cement volume growth in FY27 (Q1 domestic volume +13.1%, 81% utilisation), backed by 8.7 mt commissioned this quarter and about INR17,000 crore of projects to take capacity to 212.7 mtpa by end FY27 and about 235 mtpa by March 2028, though the brief does not give a specific FY27 revenue figure.
